title: 1978-10-10_SECTION_016_306.txt
concise_summary: PKD attempts to reconcile his two major mystical experiences (2-3-74 and 11-17-80) using Sankara's two-level theory of Brahman. He argues that what he initially interpreted as an alien intelligence (Thomas/Pigspurt) controlling him was actually accidental disinhibition caused by pentathol that gave his consciousness access to knowledge he should not have possessed, leading him to inadvertently expose this technology in the novel VALIS. The entry navigates between esoteric technological explanations and theological frameworks to make sense of agency, control, and the authorship of his own mystical writings.
key_claims: The 2-3-74 experience was not enchantment but a form of perception and knowledge-access to what an alternate consciousness (PKD2/Thomas) sees and knows
Sankara's two-level Brahman theory reconciles both 2-3-74 (nirgunam: qualityless, impersonal Absolute) and 11-17-80 (sagunam: personal Creator God) as experiences of the same divine entity

The Xerox missive contained genuine code that PKD unconsciously decoded; his decision not to respond was a conscious act that thwarted what would have been a programmed response and changed his life trajectory
VALIS was never intended to be written and published; it is the unintended result of accidental disinhibition revealing a secret revolutionary intelligence network operating on Earth
Time is real but not what ordinary consciousness assumes it to be; the experience was of set/ground discrimination that revealed Valis as camouflaged throughout the universe

tensions: Whether Valis is the Logos or something else entirely (PKD declares 'Valis is a construct and not the Logos - that's nonsense')
Control vs. free will: PKD claims to have overridden Pigspurt programming through conscious action, yet wonders if the disinhibition itself was part of a larger plan
Technology vs. theology: Framing the intelligence as technological (pentathol, mind control, telepathy) vs. theological (Brahman, Godhead, divine encounter)
Eastern vs. Western cosmology: PKD states he doesn't 'prefer' the Eastern model but his experiences seem to point toward it despite his intellectual investment in Western theology
Mental illness vs. reality: PKD's awareness that claiming alien control makes him appear psychotic, hence the religious disguise in VALIS as both cover and truth
Intentionality and authorship: PKD as novelist/reporter vs. PKD as controlled vessel; VALIS as unintended accident vs. literary achievement
The Godhead as dialectical (Hegelian) vs. Brahman's timeless transcendence: attempting to synthesize process theology with absolute non-dualism
evidence_quotes: So into my consciousness flowed priceless occult, arcane revolutionary knowledge - which, presently, I wrote up in a novel ("Valis"); but not due to my being under a control, as was the case with "Tears"!

The double superimposition of two space-times points to the projected, illusory nature of world; aspects adventitious to Brahman in itself, but there at a lower veridical level.
